text:
maria: FYI saw a spike of WS reconnects overnight where client seq numbers jumped ~2M after a proxy failover. Runtime GC evicted KV and clients rehydrated -> token spikes and higher tail latency.

chris: saw logs in eu-west too. seq baseline replay on proxy restart.

joel: root cause: proxy stores a 32-bit resume baseline. After restart it replayed an old baseline, producing huge seq_delta; GC treats that as corruption and evicts.

maria: explains doubled token usage and apdex drop.

alice: options: quick proxy-side tolerance (grace window / flag) or stronger runtime lease check before GC. Quick one is safest for UX.

joel: quick mitigation prototype:
```
if seq_delta > 1_000_000 and now - last_resume < 300s:
  session.tag = "stale-resume"
  postpone_gc(60s)
```
This avoids immediate eviction while we verify with control-plane.

chris: good but increases memory and complicates quota accounting. Suggest telemetry first: new counter `ws_seq_discontinuity.v1`.

metrics-bot: 24h: seq_discontinuities=128 global; eu-west=73, us-east=39, ap-south=16. median token spike +120%.

alice: rollout: 1) proxy patch behind feature flag, 2) add telemetry + dashboard, 3) canary in eu-west 48h, 4) follow up with runtime GC hardening. Include rollback playbook.

maria: I'll open dashboard ticket and draft playbook.

chris: quota estimator caveat: ignore single-session token blips if seq_discontinuity fired for tenant in last 2m. Joel can own.

joel: will open PRs for proxy flag and quota tweak. runtime doc after canary.

maria: thanks, will review PRs. add alert: page if `ws_seq_discontinuity` > 50 in 10m.

metrics-bot: Alert created: WS Seq Discontinuity Surge (50/10m) -> #eng-platform-oncall.

joel: PRs opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/proxy/pulls/4931 and https://git.internal/r/redwood/quota/pulls/1302. Reviews welcome.

maria: reviewing now. :thumbsup:

chris: ack
